core.duration.description: How long: a whole number and ms, s, m, h or d, as 30s, 10m or 2h

core.os.description: A machine's OS, which a box and an environment each name

core.user.description: Who a run runs as on a box: root, outside any sandbox, or a user of the box by name, lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, at most 32

env.group.description: Commands started together, each in its own sandbox, its output lines starting with its name

name.description: The group's name, unique among the stages and their members.

parallel.description:
Its members, started together, each in its own sandbox, its output
lines starting with its name.

A failing member lets its peers finish, then ends the build or job
with the first failing member's code, and later stages don't run.
A member is never a group itself, and a group has at least one. In
an environment, a group's members share their `when`, and its image
hash counts the grouping, the members' order and the group's
timeout.

items.description: One command a machine runs as it's set up, in the sandbox specification it names

timeout.description:
How long each member still running may run, within the whole
run's limit. From `1s` to `24h`.

env.ready.description: When a service is ready, which a start waits for: a port taking a connection, or a command passing, one of them

port.description: Ready once this port of the machine's loopback takes a connection.

run.description: Ready once this command line, in the service's sandbox, passes.

timeout.description: How long it's waited on before the start fails, from `1s` to `24h`.

env.secrets.description:
The secrets its runs are given, by name: their values are this
machine's, never the file's.

Each is given to the environment only once you've said yes to that
file (`lnk env approval add`), by its real path, its `name` and the
secret's ID, so a copy or a move asks again, and field flags over
it, another specification than the one you said yes to, ask for that run
alone. A missing yes is refused before the file runs, naming the
secret; `lnk env check` reads the file without one. Stages and jobs
get the values, services variables alone, and an image build none,
since an image keeps what its stages write.

names.description:
Secrets given to runs as plain variables, by name.

Each is created without `--host`; services and image builds get
none of them.

sealed.description:
Secrets the sandbox's proxy adds to requests for the host set
with each value, by name. What runs never has them.

Each is created with `--host`; stages get a placeholder, and the
proxy puts the real value in only for that host.

env.service.description: A service a machine runs beside its stages, kept running until it's stopped

name.description:
Its name, which `lnk env reset` and previews name it by.

Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, at
most 30 characters, unique among the file's services.

ready.description:
When it's ready, which a start waits for: a port taking a
connection, or a command passing.

reset.description:
A command line putting it back as the image had it, for `lnk env
reset`; none, there's nothing to run. A root service's reset runs
as root.

run.description:
A command line, for `sh -c`, that runs until it's stopped, once
its `ready` has passed.

sandbox.description:
The sandbox specification it runs in, from the file's folder.

Required for an ordinary service; one run as `root` or a named user
of the box has that user's boundary instead.

user.description:
Who it runs as; none, the machine's user.

`root`, Docker included, only on a box of its own. A service gets
the variables, and one ready on a port serves the machine's
loopback, which a sandbox reaches only where its `[localhost]
ports` lets it.

env.stage.description: One command a machine runs as it's set up, in the sandbox specification it names

inputs.description:
Files, from the file's folder, whose contents count in the image's
hash.

So a dependency lockfile makes a new image when it changes.

name.description:
Its name, unique among the file's stages and parallel members.

Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, at
most 30 characters.

sandbox.description:
The sandbox specification it runs in, from the file's folder.

Required for an ordinary stage; a root stage, or one run as a named
user of the box, has that user's boundary instead.

timeout.description:
How long it may run; none, only the build's or the job's limit.

From `1s` to `24h`, such as `30s`, `10m` or `2h`. The first limit
reached wins, and a stage past its own fails the whole build or job.

user.description:
Who it runs as; none, the machine's user.

`root` runs outside any sandbox, only while an image is built on a
box made for it, with no `sandbox` and never at every start. A user
added by `lnk box user add` runs in their own sandbox and home, with
the variables and no `sandbox`, and must exist on the box. Naming
the machine's own user is leaving it out.

when.description:
When it runs: while the image is built (`image`), saved in it, or at
every start (`start`), never saved. A root stage runs only while an
image is built.

env.step.description: A stage: one command (`run`), or a named group of commands run together (`parallel`)

oneOf.description: One command a machine runs as it's set up, in the sandbox specification it names
Commands started together, each in its own sandbox, its output lines starting with its name

description: An environment specification says what a machine has before work starts: its OS, where work starts, the values every run is given, the stages that set it up and the image they make, and the services it runs

name.description:
Its name, which its boxes and images are named by.

Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, at
most 30 characters.

os.description:
The OS its machines run; none, any, and an image for each.

`ubuntu-24.04` or `ubuntu-22.04`, as a box specification's. An OS named
refuses a box or `here` running another, a Mac included.

secrets.description:
The secrets its runs are given, by name: their values are this
machine's, never the file's.

Each is given to the environment only once you've said yes to that
file (`lnk env approval add`), by its real path, its `name` and the
secret's ID, so a copy or a move asks again, and field flags over
it, another specification than the one you said yes to, ask for that run
alone. A missing yes is refused before the file runs, naming the
secret; `lnk env check` reads the file without one. Stages and jobs
get the values, services variables alone, and an image build none,
since an image keeps what its stages write.

service.description:
The services it runs beside its stages, each kept running until
it's stopped.

items.description: A service a machine runs beside its stages, kept running until it's stopped

stage.description:
The stages, in order: the first that fails ends the build, the
start or the job, naming it.

A stage is one command, or a named group of commands run together
(`parallel`).

items.description: A stage: one command (`run`), or a named group of commands run together (`parallel`)

variables.description:
Text given to every run as it is, by name: never a secret.

Names are capital letters, digits and `_`, none of Link's (`LNK_...`,
`PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `TERM`, `LANG`, `TZ`). A
name like a secret's, such as `API_TOKEN`, is refused: a private
value is a secret, named under `[secrets]`.

version.description:
The environment file's version this Link reads, `1`.

It describes the file's shape, independently of the repository or
program versions its stages install.

workdir.description:
Where work starts, from the home folder; none, the home folder.

A relative folder, without `..`. Start stages, services, their
`ready` and `reset`, job stages and agents begin here, and it is an
agent's files folder. Image stages begin at home, so a clone can
make this folder; a later run starting before it exists fails and
names it.
